title: Science and Technology
description: Report what other people said without quoting them: the tense changes that a past reporting verb forces (present becomes past, present perfect becomes past perfect, will becomes would) and the ones a present reporting verb blocks, the modals that never move (might, could, should, must, used to), the pronouns and possessives that turn to the third person except when you report your own words, the demonstrative this that becomes that or the, the time and place words that only change because the report is made later or somewhere else, the choice between say and tell, and the word order of a reported question with if and whether; then express a gradual change with more and more or less and less before an adjective, or with the comparative repeated on both sides of and for a short adjective; and weigh an opinion, agree in part and disagree, through the vocabulary of the net and of the human being of the future (online, to surf the net, cyberspace, addict, preoccupied, conceal, relieve, irrational, aggressive, break up, survive, assume, obvious, substantial, futuristic, brains, emotions, bald)
